# 1.2.68 - the GM's browser checks the sheets and the rolls

The fourteenth stage on the way to 1.3.0 (E29), released on its own. The
primary GM's browser now judges every write a player's browser makes on that
player's own student and its items: what nothing in play covers is put back,
or shown to the GMs with Undo. A drawn roll counts only what the GMs hold;
Daggerheart now builds the drawn rolls it could not build at a table in 1.2.67.

## Before installing

1. **Nothing in the world's data moves.** There is no migration step. The
   GMs' browsers keep two new records, synced and not backed up: each
   student's sheet and module items as last judged, and a day of judged
   writes. The primary GM's first load of 1.2.68 takes each sheet as it
   finds it (read in the code). A hindering Call armed before the update
   carries no time, so it counts on the next drawn roll.
2. **Look at the world setting "Players cannot edit Actions, Hope, Health,
   Sanity or statistics".** On, the default, a player's own edits of those
   are put back or flagged, and the Party sheet's pips and the token HUD's
   bars are display-only for players; off, they are only listed. The rest,
   items and effects included, is judged either way.

## At the table, as the GM

- **There is nothing to do.** In the harness's scripted Daily Life day
  nothing the module wrote in play was put back or flagged (a table's
  evening is not measured yet).
- **Put back at once**, and the player told: a player's change to their
  student's statistics, experiences, maxima, roll rules or bonuses, Level Up
  choices, a class's hit points or the module's records; a Call added to
  those armed; Hope nothing covers; what a module item is; an effect on any
  of those or on a resource's value, or one of the module's statuses, on the
  student or its items (an item made carrying one is deleted). The GMs are
  whispered once, with each value before and after.
- **Flagged, with Undo and Keep**: a gain of Health, Sanity or actions that
  nothing in play covers; free actions or moves added by hand; a module item
  taken off, except a broken one discarded; any item added, except a
  Search's find. It stands until a GM decides, and the player is told
  nothing. The first click decides; an assistant GM's is carried out by the
  primary GM's browser. Undo makes a removed item again with its effects or
  deletes an added one, and does not write over a field changed since. A
  card older than a day says it can no longer be decided.
- **Only listed**, in `game.drpg.sheetWrites()` with a day of judged writes:
  any other field, flag, effect or item taken off, and with the setting off
  what it names. Nobody is told of these, nor of a write play covered.
- **"Sheet changes made while no GM was watching."** When the primary GM's
  world loads, or a GM takes over from a primary that left, the sheets are
  compared with the GMs' records: the card names what was put back at once,
  then each change it flags, before and after, with Undo and Keep, Undo all
  and Accept all; the rest is only listed. The card of rolls made with no
  GM connected now shows each roll's claim beside what the GM's list gives.
- **A drawn roll counts what the GMs hold.** What its window added beyond
  the list is not counted: the GMs are whispered, `rollFlags()` shows what
  was counted, and the roller is told "The GM counted ...; not counted: ...".
- **A Call that changes a roll is bought on the primary GM's browser**, for
  a player's own character too; with no GM connected it cannot be bought,
  and nothing is paid (read in the code). An Experience or an Ultimate is
  armed only with a GM's yes on its card, kept a minute by the primary GM's
  browser; a card left by a primary who has gone, or a yes lost to a reload,
  arms nothing, and the player asks again (read in the code).

## Changed

- **Drawn rolls can be built at a table.** 1.2.67 sent the GM a drawn roll
  without the data Daggerheart's roll reads when it is made (read in the
  code; such a roll, run through Daggerheart 2.10.5's roll classes outside
  Foundry, threw). The GM's browser now builds it from options of its own,
  and a request carrying any other option is refused and told.
- **One list of what may add to a drawn roll**, `LEGAL_ROLL_MODIFIERS`: the
  Hope, Fear and advantage dice, the statistic, one experience, the Calls,
  the effects that apply, Breakdown's die, the situation's dice and tools,
  the Loaded Die, the hidden stash's step and the roll's kind. A hindering
  Call counts when the roll names it or was armed over a minute before, else
  on the next roll. The record keeps the list's answer beside the claim.
- **What the GM throws is read when it throws**, after every write heard on
  that character is judged; it waits up to 16 seconds for the GM's records
  to open, or is refused: "That cannot be done now." (not measured at a
  table). A source the GM counted that the window lacked is counted with no
  line to the roller. A drawn roll's Reroll keeps what the GM counted, with
  the record's numbers rather than the sheet's.
- **The statistic.** A drawn roll of an action that lists one statistic -
  Observe, Analyze, Listen, a Palm's cover and hand, a clean-up's step, a
  crisis action such as Pin - is held to it, as a Search's was. A pick and a
  Dynamic action's difficulty count only from a GM's card, for its action
  and a statistic it lists. With no pick, the lowest one listed is thrown,
  the GMs told, and the roller that the one claimed was not counted. A
  clean-up said to come through the Tamper tile is held to Tamper's
  statistic only for a roller who is not Stage 6's cleaner, whose erase
  waits for the GM's pick.
- **Calls.** An armed Call a player's browser adds is put back and never
  counted; each armed Call now carries the time it was armed. A hindering
  Call, or one the GM armed, that a player's browser takes off with no roll
  of theirs is put back, and the player told. A Call bought on the GM, a
  drawn roll's Hope and every Hope a Reroll moves are paid from what the GMs
  hold, after every write heard on that character is judged.
- **A gain stands as far as play covers it**: a refund of what was paid in
  the last 30 minutes, a Rest, an item used and, for free actions and moves,
  a Call's grant. Hope beyond it is put back as a difference: Hope spent at
  once still costs, a later change is kept. A GM's refund of Hope and a
  Reroll's give-back of Sanity or Health use up their payment's credit, so a
  second refund is put back or flagged as that resource is; a Reroll's
  take-back leaves none; no credit passes the GMs' maximum. Daggerheart's
  requests to the GM for a player's student give Hope only as far as a roll of
  theirs from the last minute covers it, and only lower a module item's count,
  never above what the GMs hold (not tried at a table).
- **What is judged.** A write replacing or deleting an entire part of a
  sheet or an item is judged field by field, and an effect written through
  its student's or item's update, or an item through its student's, as one
  written on its own. So is what a Truth Bullet says or is, in whatever
  form it is written - through its student's update, or with the module's
  flags replaced or deleted whole: a player's edit is put back once the
  rest of that write is judged, and a GM's goes to the trace it came from.
  A character's writes are judged in turn, each as made; a put-back writes
  back only what the sheet still holds of its write, an Undo of a Rest its
  stamp exactly. When a player asks for a hand-over, a loot, a theft, a
  plant or an Analyze, the GM's browser reads the item or Truth Bullet as
  the GMs hold it, not as a write still waiting for its put-back left it.
  So it does where it decides by a student's items: a crisis swing, a tool's
  relief on a Work or a Sabotage, a receiver's carry limit, an item used,
  the Rot's wear, a GM's ruling on an item, a drawn roll's situation die, a
  clean-up's Cleaning Tool, what a discovery, a close or a use breaks, an
  Objection's evidence, the object whose traces a swing ties to the crime,
  and a Reroll's find, its replayed use and the plant it takes back and
  gives again. A Reroll's take-backs read what they give back as the GMs
  hold it: a used item's charge, the Hope a use gave, and the maximum the
  marks put back stop at. A death and a chapter's end sweep the Truth
  Bullets as the GMs hold them, and a player's deletion of one they take
  is kept, so that no Undo makes it again. A GM's give or take of a
  student's actions, Hope or marks, and a Level Up, read the value and the
  maximum as the GMs hold them, not a player's write the audit has not put
  back yet. Daggerheart's scars, which set Hope's maximum, are judged as the
  fields only a GM writes: put back with the setting on or off, an effect on
  them taken off; a roll's marks are held to the maxima the GMs hold; a
  Level Up rises from the sheet's values as the GMs hold them, not from what
  Daggerheart prepares from them. A Reroll's price given back and a
  critical's second Hope stop at the Hope maximum the GMs hold.
- **Items.** A module item's category, tier, identity, roles and usable kind
  stay as made; mending a broken one, lowering its wear (read in the code) or
  raising its count is put back. A broken weapon is swung by nobody, readied
  again or not. A bedroom key's room is a GM's to write: a player's write of
  one is put back and the GMs told, and a hand-over or a plant of the item it
  was written on makes nobody a key. An item a player made on a sheet changes
  no hands - given, looted, planted or stolen - until a GM keeps it or its
  record is swept (after a day) or, read in the code, reset; undone, it is
  gone. A move into or out of a stash stands when the GM's browser sees the
  student in that stash's room, with room in the stash or under the carry
  limit. A usable keeps the kind it was made with; a GM's edit of the item
  tables reaches items made after it (read in the code). A Search's find
  stands only when the GM spent that Search's token.
- **The GMs' records keep up.** The primary GM's browser fills those of a
  new character and those a reset takes, and lists a player's write on a
  student it holds no record of.
- **Setting a student up and restoring a starting sheet are a GM's**, as
  the roads a table uses already were (read in the code).
- **What each browser holds.** Each judged write sends the GMs' browsers
  one patch of their record: 115 in one run of the harness's scripted Daily
  Life day, 35 of them for items. A module write names its reason from one
  closed list, sent only with a player's write the GMs judge and with the
  audit's own. A player's browser keeps nothing new.

## Known gaps

- The GMs' list was switched on from the harness's explanation of each kind
  of flag 1.2.67 raised, not from a table's `rollFlags()`: a source missing
  from it would show as "not counted", to the GMs and the roller at once.
- Rolls the GM does not draw are not held to the list: with no GM, on a
  Daggerheart build whose rolls stay in the players' browsers, and
  Daggerheart's item and damage rolls; their Reroll adds none of the
  effects Daggerheart 2.10.5 would (read in the code).
- Rolls with no action of their own - hiding a murder's traces, concealing
  a sabotage or a clean-up, a broken item's - use their window's statistic,
  and a clean-up's roll the step its window names (read in the code).
- A hindering Call or one the GM armed, spent on a roll the GM does not
  draw, stays spent only if that roll's card reaches the chat within two
  seconds (chosen, not measured); a roll with no card of its own covers none
  (read in the code).
- A Daggerheart item that is not the module's, taken off by its owner, is
  listed, not flagged, even with an effect that counted: the GMs hold no
  copy of it to make again (read in the code).
- What Daggerheart's own character creation, level-up or reset writes from
  a player's browser to statistics, experiences or bonuses is put back as a
  hand edit would be (read in the code; whether it does is not measured).
- The away card is only as good as the returning GM's browser's records: one
  that never held them takes the sheets as it finds them (read in the code).
- An effect on the scars, in the moment before the audit puts a player's
  back, sets the maximum a GM's give-back stops at (modelled in the harness,
  which applies no effects; not measured at a table).
- A reaction requested from the chat shows no success line on its card
  (read in the code).

## Checked

- The headless suite, run as `npm test` on this release's code (commit
  0fa68c3: the tree that ships but for the version stamps, these notes, four
  handbook asides and the ledger's row): 863 passed, 0 failed, 17 skipped
  (738 at 1.2.67). New in the suite: R220, R221 and R290, and the tier-2
  tests of each fix. The scenarios: 17 of 17 green; 72's three expected reds
  stand (S17-31 until E43, a Foundry limit, S17-64 until E60). The suite
  takes about 26 minutes on the test machine, the whole of `npm test` 42.
- The Polish file's prose check: 497 of 497 strings covered, missing 0,
  extra 0.
- Before this commit, the stage's five verify sentences and four doneWhen
  clauses were each matched to the test or scenario check that answers
  them: seven by the suite and the scenarios above, one only at a table
  (the Party sheet and the token bar as a player, and a chapter with no
  false subtraction: LIVE-E29-02 and -03), one in part (a bare advantage
  die with no Call behind it has no test of its own). These notes and the
  changed handbook lines were then read once more against those tests;
  six sentences were cut to what the logs support, four handbook lines
  say they are a reading or a table check.
- The harness now builds a drawn roll from what Daggerheart's roll reads,
  and the module as it was before this release's fix fails there.
  Daggerheart 2.10.5's own roll classes, run outside Foundry on the rolls
  the harness sent, threw on that module and build them now.
- An independent review in two rounds (security, and whether the change is
  correct and its tests measure); its findings were fixed in nine commits
  after each round. One more after the first holds an action that lists
  one statistic to it (an auditor's note), and seventeen more after the
  second close gaps the fixes themselves found.
- Not checked in a real Foundry yet: a chapter with a GM and two players,
  with no false put-back, card or "not counted" and `sheetWrites()` and
  `rollFlags()` read at its end; the Party sheet and token bars as a player;
  Daggerheart's own item delete and add; two GMs on one card; the away card;
  a sheet statistic's card; Daggerheart 2.6.5 and the current 2.10.9; Dice
  So Nice; a write's reason reaching the primary GM on Foundry 13 and 14; a
  drawn roll's card and a GM's pick card; an assistant GM's yes; a primary
  leaving; the waits a drawn roll takes; effects and items as Foundry 14
  and Daggerheart write them; a Search's find - the audit's live checks,
  section 9.2, items 110 to 124 (LIVE-E29-01 to 15). The local release gate
  needs a local Foundry v14 and did not run for this release.
